intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that dystonia-25 (DYT25) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GNAL gene on chromosome 18p.

checks.claim: Dystonia-25 (DYT25) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GNAL gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Since dystonia is rare and inherited in an AD manner in these pedigrees, the causative mutation is expected to be an extremely rare heterozygous variant, shared by all affected family members.
checks.explanation: The paper identifies heterozygous GNAL mutations as the cause of primary torsion dystonia. DYT25 is the standard name for this disorder.

paragraphs.text: Dystonia-25 is a form of primary torsion dystonia, in which dystonia, with or without tremor, is the only neurologic sign. It usually begins in adulthood, although onset ranges from childhood to the sixth decade. Onset is most often in the neck. The dystonia frequently spreads to other sites, especially the cranial muscles, and speech is often affected (Bressman et al., 1994; Fuchs et al., 2013).

paragraphs.text: Fuchs et al. (2013) reported 28 individuals with definite dystonia and complete clinical information from 8 multiplex families with primary torsion dystonia who carried GNAL mutations. All were Caucasian of mixed European ancestry. Mean age at dystonia onset was 31.3 years (range, 7 to 54 years). Onset was in the neck in 82% of carriers, and 93% had neck involvement at final examination. Most patients had progressed to dystonia at other sites, and only 46% had focal dystonia at last examination. Cranial involvement was present in 57% of carriers and speech involvement in 44%. No patient had brachial onset, and only 32% eventually had arm involvement. Other sites of onset included the legs, larynx, jaw, and tongue, and a few patients developed generalized dystonia. Phenotypes varied within families carrying the same mutation. Dystonia was inherited from the maternal and paternal sides equally, and Fuchs et al. (2013) saw no apparent phenotypic differences between maternally and paternally inherited cases.

paragraphs.text: Fuchs et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing in 2 families with autosomal dominant primary torsion dystonia. In family P, which was of mixed Russian and Swiss Mennonite heritage, they identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation in the GNAL gene (S293X) in a linkage region. The mutation segregated with dystonia in the family. In family D1 they identified a heterozygous missense mutation in GNAL (V137M) that segregated with the disease. Neither variant was found in about 3,500 European exomes in the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project database, and V137M was not found in 572 control chromosomes.

paragraphs.text: Fuchs et al. (2013) then Sanger-sequenced the coding region of GNAL in 39 additional multiplex families with primary torsion dystonia of mixed European origin who were negative for DYT1 and DYT6 mutations. They found novel heterozygous GNAL mutations in 6 families (19%): a nonsense mutation (R21X), 2 frameshift mutations (S95fsX110 and R198fsX210), a missense mutation (E155K), an in-frame deletion of 3 amino acids (P102-V104del), and a possible splice site mutation (c.274-5T-C). Bioinformatic analysis suggested that the c.274-5T-C change disrupts an acceptor splice site, but Fuchs et al. (2013) could not confirm this because GNAL expression was undetectable in patient lymphoblasts. None of the variants were found in dbSNP135, about 3,500 European exomes, or 572 control chromosomes. The mutations segregated with the disease in all families for which DNA from multiple affected individuals was available. The V137 and E155 residues were completely conserved in GNAL orthologs. In a cell-based BRET assay of Gα-olf coupling to the dopamine D1 receptor, the S293X mutant failed to support any receptor-driven responses. The E155K and V137M mutants showed intermediate phenotypes, largely consistent with impaired association with the G-beta-gamma subunits. A V16F variant found in a single control showed wildtype-like behavior. Fuchs et al. (2013) concluded that the functional assay suggested loss of function, and they predicted that the early truncating mutations would remove essential functional regions of the protein.

paragraphs.text: Fuchs et al. (2013) noted that GNAL encodes Gα-olf, a stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit. In striatal medium spiny neurons, Gα-olf replaces Gα-s and couples dopamine D1 receptors and adenosine A2A receptors to the activation of adenylyl cyclase type 5. Fuchs et al. (2013) proposed that GNAL mutations point to primary abnormalities of D1 receptor and/or A2A receptor transmission as a cause of dystonia. In this model, the primary abnormality lies postsynaptically, in striatal dopaminoceptive neurons and/or cholinergic interneurons.

paragraphs.text: Fuchs et al. (2013) used exome sequencing in a family with primary torsion dystonia of mixed Russian and Swiss Mennonite heritage (family P) and identified a heterozygous c.878C-A transversion in the GNAL gene, resulting in a ser293-to-ter (S293X) substitution. The mutation lay within a linkage region and segregated with dystonia in the family. It was not found in about 3,500 European exomes in the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project database. In a BRET assay, the S293X mutant failed to support any dopamine D1 receptor-driven responses. Affected family members had ages at onset of 25 to 48 years. Onset was in the neck in most of them, and 2 had generalized dystonia.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with primary torsion dystonia (family T), Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous c.61C-T transition in the GNAL gene, resulting in an arg21-to-ter (R21X) substitution. The variant was not found in dbSNP135, about 3,500 European exomes, or 572 control chromosomes. Fuchs et al. (2013) predicted that the mutant transcript is likely degraded by nonsense-mediated decay. Two family members had neck-onset dystonia, and 1 had laryngeal onset.

checks.claim: Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous c.61C-T transition in the GNAL gene in affected members of primary torsion dystonia family T.
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY T | | | | | | c.61C>T | p.R21X

checks.claim: The GNAL c.61C-T transition results in an arg21-to-ter (R21X) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY T | | | | | | c.61C>T | p.R21X

checks.claim: The GNAL R21X variant was not found in dbSNP135, about 3,500 European exomes, or 572 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: None of the variants were detected in dbSNP135, ~3,500 European exomes or 572 control chromosomes that we tested.

checks.claim: Fuchs et al. (2013) predicted that the GNAL R21X mutant transcript is likely degraded by nonsense-mediated decay.
checks.evidence_quote: In addition, p.R21X is likely degraded by nonsense mediated decay thus producing no protein.

checks.claim: Two members of family T with the GNAL R21X mutation had neck-onset dystonia.
checks.explanation: T-1 and T-2 had neck onset.

checks.claim: One member of family T with the GNAL R21X mutation had laryngeal-onset dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: 3 | F | 25 | 33 | S | Larynx | |

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with primary torsion dystonia (family D2), Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous 1-bp insertion (c.283-284insT) in the GNAL gene, predicted to result in a frameshift and premature termination (S95fsX110). The variant was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes. The 4 affected women had ages at onset of 11 to 39 years. Sites of onset included the neck, jaw, and tongue.

checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY D2 | | | | | | c.283-284insT | p.S95fsX110

checks.claim: The GNAL c.283-284insT insertion is predicted to result in a frameshift and premature termination (S95fsX110).
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY D2 | | | | | | c.283-284insT | p.S95fsX110
checks.explanation: Stated in Table 1; the text calls it a frameshift.

checks.claim: The GNAL c.283-284insT variant was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: None of the variants were detected in dbSNP135, ~3,500 European exomes or 572 control chromosomes that we tested.

checks.claim: Family D2 with the GNAL S95fsX110 mutation had 4 affected women.
checks.evidence_quote: 4 | F | 11 | 19 | F | Tongue | |

checks.claim: Sites of dystonia onset in family D2 with the GNAL S95fsX110 mutation included the neck, jaw, and tongue.
checks.explanation: Family D2 onset sites are neck, jaw, neck and tongue.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with primary torsion dystonia (family N), Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous 9-bp deletion (c.304-312delCCTCCAGTT) in the GNAL gene, resulting in an in-frame deletion of 3 amino acids (P102-V104del). The deletion was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes. The patient, a man, had onset of focal neck dystonia at age 20 years.

checks.claim: Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous 9-bp deletion (c.304-312delCCTCCAGTT) in the GNAL gene in a patient with primary torsion dystonia from family N.
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY N | | | | | | c.304-312delCCTCCAGTT | p.P102-V104del

checks.claim: The GNAL c.304-312delCCTCCAGTT deletion results in an in-frame deletion of 3 amino acids (P102-V104del).
checks.evidence_quote: one in-frame deletion of 3 amino acids (p.P102-V104del)

checks.claim: The GNAL c.304-312delCCTCCAGTT deletion was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: None of the variants were detected in dbSNP135, ~3,500 European exomes or 572 control chromosomes that we tested.

checks.claim: The family N patient with the GNAL P102-V104del mutation was a man.
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists this patient as male.

checks.claim: The family N patient with the GNAL P102-V104del mutation had onset of focal neck dystonia at age 20 years.
checks.explanation: Table 1 gives onset at 20 years, focal distribution and neck site.

paragraphs.text: In 2 affected members of a family with primary torsion dystonia (family S), Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous c.463G-A transition in the GNAL gene, resulting in a glu155-to-lys (E155K) substitution at a residue completely conserved in GNAL orthologs. The variant was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes. In a BRET assay, the mutant showed an intermediate phenotype, largely consistent with impaired association with G-beta-gamma subunits. Both patients had neck-onset dystonia at ages 17 and 18 years.

checks.claim: Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous c.463G-A transition in the GNAL gene in 2 affected members of primary torsion dystonia family S.
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY S* | | | | | | c.463G>A | p.E155K
checks.explanation: Table 1 lists 2 affected family S members.

checks.claim: The GNAL c.463G-A transition results in a glu155-to-lys (E155K) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: FAMILY S* | | | | | | c.463G>A | p.E155K

checks.claim: GNAL residue E155 is completely conserved in GNAL orthologs.
checks.evidence_quote: The p.V137 and p.E155 residues were completely conserved in GNAL orthologs (Fig. 1b).

checks.claim: The GNAL E155K variant was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: None of the variants were detected in dbSNP135, ~3,500 European exomes or 572 control chromosomes that we tested.

checks.claim: In a BRET assay, the GNAL E155K mutant showed an intermediate phenotype largely consistent with impaired association with G-beta-gamma subunits.
checks.evidence_quote: Two mutants found in dystonia patients, p.E155K and p.V137M, showed intermediate phenotypes largely consistent with impaired association with the Gβγ subunits (Fig. 2).

checks.claim: Both affected members of family S with the GNAL E155K mutation had neck-onset dystonia.
checks.explanation: Both family S members had neck onset.

checks.claim: The 2 affected members of family S with the GNAL E155K mutation had dystonia onset at ages 17 and 18 years.
checks.explanation: Table 1 gives onset ages of 18 and 17.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with primary torsion dystonia (family H), Fuchs et al. (2013) identified a heterozygous 1-bp insertion (c.591-592insA) in the GNAL gene, predicted to result in a frameshift and premature termination (R198fsX210). The variant was not found in control databases or 572 control chromosomes. The 3 affected members had focal neck dystonia with onset at ages 31 to 47 years.

The 3 affected members of family H with the GNAL R198fsX210 mutation had focal neck dystonia.
checks.explanation: All 3 family H members have focal dystonia with neck onset.

checks.claim: The 3 affected members of family H with the GNAL R198fsX210 mutation had dystonia onset at ages 31 to 47 years.
